title: Pounce helps incoming students complete college enrollment
summary: AdmitHub’s text-message assistant Pounce raised enrollment by 3.3 percentage points among students already committed to Georgia State in 2016.
account: Georgia State University used AdmitHub’s Pounce to help admitted students complete enrollment tasks from April through August 2016. Researchers assigned 7,489 students to the assistant or to usual support. Pounce used university records to send relevant reminders, answered questions and referred unresolved questions to counselors. Among 1,948 students who had already committed to attend, the researchers found that enrollment increased by 3.3 percentage points from a control rate of 84.6%. The overall enrollment effect was not statistically significant. The study evaluated the complete service, including staff assistance. It did not measure degree completion. In two later randomized trials with enrolled students at a two-year and a four-year college, Page, Meyer, Lee and Gehlbach found that chatbot outreach worked best for discrete and time-sensitive tasks such as filing financial aid forms or registering for courses (EdWorkingPaper, August 2023). Georgia State’s research partnership with Mainstay (formerly AdmitHub) continued. In two randomized trials of course-specific Pounce chatbots in introductory courses, Meyer and colleagues found that the chatbot raised the share of students who earned a course grade of B or higher by 5 to 6 percentage points and reduced course drops (EdWorkingPaper 22-564, revised September 2023).
purpose: Georgia State deployed Pounce to guide admitted students through the tasks that they had to complete before enrollment. The intended result was higher on-time enrollment.
system: Pounce, AdmitHub’s SMS assistant with supervised learning and a Georgia State knowledge base
segment: College transition support for admitted students

ai_role.statement: Pounce interpreted questions, sent reminders, and routed questions that it could not answer to university staff. The trial measured the combined service, not machine learning alone.
